issues.description: Stock class method naming mismatch: the problem statement UML (and the solution implementation) declare a method named emptyStock() for clearing the stock, while the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This is a naming inconsistency for the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock). As a result, students reading the specification or using instructor tests that expect emptyStock() will not find that method in the template and may be unable to compile or will be confused about which method to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (public void emptyStock()) so the template matches the problem statement and solution, or add a new public method emptyStock() that delegates to clearInventory() (e.g., public void emptyStock() { clearInventory(); }). Ensure the method signature is public void emptyStock() so student code and tests that call emptyStock() compile and behave as expected.
